newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukrainian oil refinery needs state help for debt.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian oil refinery needs state help for debt.

text.p: Ukraine's troubled Lisichansk oil refinery can restructure its debt to Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank only if the Ukrainian government provides guarantees, the State Property Fund said on Thursday.

"As soon as Ukraine's government provides guarantees for the loan, the German bank would agree to restructure it over the next eight years," said fund chairman Yuri Yekhanurov, who heads the state privatisation body.
He did not say whether such state support was forthcoming.
Lisichansk (now AT Lisichansknaftosyntez) owes the bank $70 million for a 1993 loan, received under government guarantees.
Yekhanurov said previously that a 45 percent stake in the refinery, Ukraine's second largest, would be made available for strategic investor.
The Lisichansk refinery, located 500 km east of Kiev near the Russian border, has an annual capacity of 16 million tonnes.
According to the Statistics Ministry, Lisichansk processed only 1.80 million tonnes of oil in the first 10 months of 1996.

Ukraine's refineries routinely processed 60 million tonnes (equivalent to around 1.2 million barrels per day) of crude oil a year in Soviet times, but they refined only 13.4 million tonnes (268,000 bpd) last year, compared to 16.8 million tonnes in 1995.
The forecast for this year is 22 million tonnes (440,000 bpd).
